message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE in the current auction.

I have $373 cash and several properties. The current high bid is $150 by p4, requiring a minimum next bid of $151. I am weighing whether to enter this auction.

I considered the cash impact of buying. It would leave $73 and mortgages totaling $395, barely covering light-blue hotels or Baltic Avenue. I also noted that p4 would still need Pacific from p3 to complete the green set.

p3 is cash-poor with only $157, while p4 has $889 and light-blue hotels. A $151 bid would leave me with $222, which is too little to cover the light-blue hotels or Baltic Avenue. I am now calculating mortgage values for my properties to see if I can raise the cash needed.

I recalculated the mortgageable value of my properties. It totals $305, not the $395 I had previously estimated. I am now questioning whether the game uses different mortgage values than standard Monopoly rules.

Mortgaging all remaining properties yields $678 in total cash. That still cannot cover both a light-blue hotel and Baltic Avenue.

A $151 bid would leave me with $527, still short of the $550–$600 light-blue hotel rents. I cannot afford to buy a property that does not complete my set. Denying p4 is also pointless because they already own Pennsylvania.

I am dropping out of the auction. p3 is bidding on Pacific, which they need to complete their set too. I cannot afford to compete.

Bidding would drain my cash into the bank and leave me weaker. p4 has $889 and will likely raise further, so I cannot afford to outbid them.
